title: UK economy grows 0.7% in third quarter, led by tech services
h1: The UK economy grew 0.7% in the third quarter, led by technology services, keeping a December rate rise in play
description: UK GDP rose 0.7% in July to September 2026, the ONS said November 12. Information and communication output grew 2.1% while construction fell 0.7%.
standfirst: Britain's first estimate for the quarter matched forecasts and beat the spring's pace. Services did nearly all the work, and builders went backwards.
keywords: UK GDP Q3 2026, UK economy third quarter 2026, ONS GDP first quarterly estimate, Bank of England December rate hike, UK services growth, UK construction output
takeaways: UK real GDP rose 0.7% in July to September 2026, up from 0.5% in the second quarter, and was 1.9% higher than a year earlier.
Services grew 0.9% and information and communication 2.1%; production rose 0.1% and construction fell 0.7%.
Markets put the chance of a Bank of England rate rise in December at 73%. The next GDP release is due December 22.
body: The United Kingdom's economy grew 0.7% in the three months from July to September, faster than the 0.5% recorded in the second quarter, the Office for National Statistics said in its first estimate on Thursday, November 12. Output was 1.9% higher than in the same quarter of 2025. Economists polled by Reuters had expected 0.7%, CNBC reported.

Almost all of it came from services, which grew 0.9%. Services sold to businesses rose 1.0% and those sold to consumers 0.5%, the statistics office said. The information and communication sector grew 2.1%. The office said that sector has been the biggest driver of growth this year, with many fast-growing firms tied to artificial intelligence and cloud computing, though it added that the exact effect of those activities is hard to measure, according to CNBC.

The rest of the economy was weaker. Production output edged up 0.1% after a 0.1% fall in the spring. Construction output fell 0.7% and was 1.7% lower than a year earlier. Real GDP per head rose 0.7% in the quarter.
A separate monthly estimate published the same day showed the economy grew 0.2% in September. August was revised down to no growth from 0.1%.
What does it mean for interest rates?

The Bank of England raised interest rates last week for the first time in three years and warned that more increases could follow if the U.S.-Iran war is not resolved, CNBC reported. UK annual inflation rose to 3.5% in September. Markets were pricing a 73% chance of another increase at the bank's December meeting, CNBC said, citing LSEG data. The pound slipped 0.2% against the dollar on Thursday morning.
Chancellor John Healey said the figures showed "stand-out resilience," according to CNBC. The bank's own November forecast projects slower growth in the fourth quarter and into 2027.

These are early figures and can be revised. The statistics office's next quarterly GDP release is scheduled for December 22, after the government's Autumn Budget and the Bank of England's final rate decision of the year.
